citations.title: IDF says Gaza strike killed two terrorists working for Doctors Without Borders
citations.excerpt: The military says it killed two terrorists who were working as members of the Doctors Without Borders (MSF) group in an airstrike in Gaza City. According to the Israel Defense Forces, terrorists Ahmed Safian Muhammad Ali Abu Hasirah and Ma’ad Yousef Alisbah, a commander of an artillery squad in the Hamas military wing, worked as watchmen for an MSF clinic. The IDF says contrary to claims, it did not target a hospital and no damage was caused to medical infrastructure. MSF says the organization is “devastated and outraged by the killing of two of our colleagues, both watchmen, in an Israeli strike on one of our Gaza clinics tonight.” “This is a direct hit on MSF, bringing the total number of MSF colleagues killed in Gaza to 17. Our premises were clearly marked with MSF logos, and their location had been communicated to and was known by the Israeli military. We stand in solidarity with the families and loved ones of our colleagues. We call for accountability,” it says in a statement. The medical organization has repeatedly denied that it employs members of terror groups despite overwhelming evidence to the contrary.

passages.text: On Friday evening, the IDF carried out a precision strike in Gaza City targeting two Hamas military wing operatives who were employed as security guards at a clinic run by Doctors Without Borders. The military said the men had been advancing attack plans against Israeli forces and civilians.

The IDF identified the eliminated individuals as Ahmed Sufyan Muhammad Ali Abu Hasira and Moaz Yousef Alitsbach, the latter an artillery unit commander in Hamas’s military wing. The IDF emphasized that the strike did not target a hospital and caused no damage to medical infrastructure.

MSF responded by stating that the strike constituted a direct hit on its premises, bringing the number of its staff killed in Gaza to 17, and called for accountability while noting that the clinic’s location and markings had been communicated to the IDF.

The Israel Defense Forces stated that the two men were Hamas terrorists operating under the cover of humanitarian employment at the MSF clinic and that they were eliminated to remove the threat they posed to Israeli civilians and IDF troops after advancing attack plans.

The discrepancy between the IDF’s description of the targets as Hamas operatives using humanitarian cover and MSF’s characterization of the strike as a direct hit on a marked medical facility continues to drive competing narratives on social media and in international coverage.
